title: Image security: vulnerability scanning and provenance

videos.script: An image is software somebody else mostly wrote. This lesson asks two questions about it: what is known to be wrong with it, and where did it come from. {{scan}} A scanner lists every package and module, and looks each one up. Debian slim: a hundred and sixty three findings. Alpine: none. Shelf: two. {{triage}} Most of Debian's have no fix yet, so rebuilding would change nothing. Shelf's high one does have a fix: one Go module, one version up. Ana updates it, rebuilds, and scans again. {{attest}} Then the build writes down its own answers: a bill of materials, and a statement of the base images and the commit it was built from. They travel with the image, in the same registry.
